factors.factor: Mismatch between the IPC Template Type definition (expecting 21 inputs) and the sensor code that supplied only 20 input values; the defect was latent and not caught because no prior channel file used the 21st input.
factors.evidence: "The definition of the IPC Template Type in the Template Type Definitions file stated that it expected 21 input fields. The sensor code that invoked the Content Interpreter with Channel File 291's Template Instances supplied only 20 input values to match against."

factors.factor: Testing did not exercise the code path that failed: the automated test set used a static channel file with wildcard matching in the 21st field, so the non-wildcard comparison against the 21st input was never tested.
factors.evidence: "a static set of 12 test cases was selected. A channel file was defined manually for use within these test cases, and it used a regex wildcard matching criterion in the 21st field for all Template Instances."

factors.factor: Testing was focused on functional validation and did not include fuzzing or adversarial input-boundary testing of the Content Interpreter's handling of input counts.
factors.evidence: "Manual and automated testing were performed during development, focused on functional validation: the correct flow of security-relevant data through the Template Type and the generation of appropriate detection alerts."

factors.factor: The stress test used a test Template Instance that did not reproduce the failing condition, giving false assurance that the Template Type was safe for use.
factors.evidence: "The IPC Template Type was stress tested with a test Template Instance in a test environment consisting of a variety of operating systems and workloads. It passed the stress test and was validated for use."

factors.factor: The Content Validator checked channel files against the 21-input definition rather than against the inputs the sensor actually supplies, so it passed content that would crash the sensor.
factors.evidence: "The Content Validator evaluated the new Template Instances. It based its assessment on the expectation that the IPC Template Type would be provided with 21 inputs."

factors.factor: Rapid Response Content is delivered as configuration data without the same staged rollout, canary, or safety gating applied to code, so a faulty channel file reached the full sensor population at once.
factors.evidence: "Rapid Response Content is configuration data; it is not code or a kernel driver." and "The new Template Instances were sent to sensors."

factors.factor: Memory-safety weakness in the kernel driver: the code read the input at index 0x14 without a bounds check, so a malformed count produced an invalid memory read in kernel space rather than a graceful rejection.
factors.evidence: "The code read the input at index 0x14 (the 21st element), which did not point to valid memory. The code performed a NULL pointer check, then read through the invalid pointer, resulting in the out-of-bounds read and the bugcheck."

factors.factor: Kernel-mode placement of a driver that evaluates externally delivered content amplified the impact, since a fault crashes the whole system and boot-time loading can prevent recovery without manual intervention.
factors.evidence: "The Falcon sensor uses a kernel driver (csagent.sys), loaded from an early phase of system boot so the sensor can observe and defend against malware that launches before user mode processes start."

factors.factor: Recovery was slow and effectively manual at scale, with roughly 99% of sensors back only about ten days after the update.
factors.evidence: "As of July 29 at 5 p.m. PT, using a week-over-week comparison, ~99% of Windows sensors were online compared to before the content update (typical week-over-week variance is ~1%)."
